prior_year_events.impact_description: Exposure to war on land and contingent aviation war and hull coverage for lessors; booked ultimates as at 31 December 2023 of GBP 51.7m gross and GBP 21.3m net (inclusive of inwards and outwards RIPs).
Largest catastrophe loss in the syndicate in 2022 calendar year; uncertainty reduced in 2023 as claims developed during the year.
Material exposure to a series of MidWest storms; sensitivity noted that a 25% deterioration on selected gross ultimate would have a modest net impact on 2022 YOA.

named_events.loss_description: Hurricane Ian was the largest catastrophe loss in the syndicate in 2022 calendar year, however in 2023 uncertainty was reduced due to the claims developing in the year.
Material exposure to a series of MidWest storms; a 25% deterioration on the current selected gross ultimate loss pick was modelled as an example.

data.standardized_narrative: At 31 December 2023 the syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding were GBP 383.6m. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle shows no material aggregate prior-year development across the older underwriting years (net movement ~GBP 0.0m), i.e. reserves were broadly stable on a gross basis. The syndicate continues to carry exposures to natural catastrophe losses (notably prior Hurricane Ian and a series of MidWest storms) and geopolitical losses arising from the Russia-Ukraine conflict (booked gross ultimates GBP 51.7m, net GBP 21.3m). Management explicitly allowed for economic and excess inflation and uplifted IBNR and case reserves where appropriate; these reserving adjustments were documented in the reserving notes but did not produce a net aggregate prior year strengthening or release at year-end.
raw_causal_phrases: The 2021 and 2022 YOA have material exposure to Russia-Ukraine which is currently very difficult to quantify.
The booked ultimates for these losses as at 31 December 2023 are GBP 51.7 million gross of reinsurance and GBP 21.3 million net of reinsurance (inclusive of inwards and outwards RIPs).
Hurricane Ian was the largest catastrophe loss in the syndicate in 2022 calendar year, however in 2023 uncertainty was reduced due to the claims developing in the year.
We have explicitly considered economic and excess inflation in the reserving process when setting the best estimate reserves.
Uplifting outstanding claims reserves by a set factor (at class of business underwriting year level).
For IBNR claims the Managing Agent has uplifted the initial expected loss ratios ("IELRs") used in the reserving model.
data.data_quality_notes: No explicit single-line 'movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding (gross)' figure was presented; net prior-year phrases in the narrative were typically net of reinsurance. Prior-year development was therefore derived from the gross claims development table (triangle) which shows effectively no aggregate movement for underwriting years up to 2021. A post-balance-sheet RITC (Syndicate 3268) was completed on 9 Feb 2024 which transfers reserves and may distort comparisons after year-end; that RITC is a post-balance-sheet event and is not included in the 31 Dec 2023 positions.
